=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Edinburgh prisoner report, 1767 ===
An Edinburgh city-gaol report names Robert Glasgow among prisoners convicted of theft and reports their sentence of public exposure and banishment from the city and liberties forever.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395727807/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1767-12-21, p.3].</ref>

The report gives no age, family or later outcome identifying the prisoner. It does not establish that he was Robert, son of Andrew the Calder miller, named in 1772.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2473]]. Uncertain birth before 7 January 1703 at Edinburgh permits an older adult in 1767. This upper birth bound is not an exact baptism or age; no court or banishment identification.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, master of John and Archibald, 1754 ===
Robert Glasgow, master of the snow John and Archibald, of Glasgow, is reported arriving in distress during a Virginia-to-Glasgow passage.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398244/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1754-03-19, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971274921/ The Gloucester Journal, 1754-06-25, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1212017118/ Berrow’s Worcester Journal, 1754-06-27, p.1].</ref>

These are reprints of one shipping report. "Of Glasgow" describes the vessel; John and Archibald is its name, not two relatives of the master.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2473]]. Chronologically possible (at least 51); no corroborating maritime evidence. Cited sources cites a Findmypast baptism transcript dated 7 Jan 1703 at Edinburgh; maintained vital preserves the before qualifier. The family account link the baptism to Edinburgh parents, but no relevant maritime or London criminal record was identified.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Old Bailey and Newgate reports, 1751 ===
Robert Glasgow is reported among nine Old Bailey convicts receiving judgment of death, for highway robbery of Joseph Weedon’s gold ring, silver shoe buckles and other things.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971486582/ The Gloucester Journal, 1751-07-16, p.2].</ref>

Robert Glasgow, condemned for robbing Joseph Weedon on the highway, is included among Newgate prisoners ordered for execution on Monday next.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979343886/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury, 1751-07-29, p.2].</ref>

The judgment and later order for execution are separate reports. An order for execution is not proof that it occurred; neither report supplies the relatives or origin needed to identify Robert among the Scottish namesakes.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2473]]. Chronologically possible (at least 48); no corroborating London evidence. Cited sources cites a Findmypast baptism transcript dated 7 Jan 1703 at Edinburgh; maintained vital preserves the before qualifier. The family account link the baptism to Edinburgh parents, but no relevant maritime or London criminal record was identified.
